notes: Configs are planning PROCESSES, not skill vs no-skill: 'incremental' reveals one stage at a time (RL 3, quant 6); 'all_at_once' states every goal in message 1. Same skills, same persona, n=1 each — treat differences as directional.

Blind judge (final docs only): RL all-at-once 8.9 vs incremental 7.1; Quant all-at-once 9.1 vs incremental 5.7. Incremental had deeper technical/statistical detail both times but lost on consistency, size and stale text.

Root cause #1 — the brief never re-aims. New-mode briefs bake stage-1 features into goals (RL Goal 5 'The first game, Snake, teaches…'); later fit-checks then say 'serves existing goal' so the brief stays stage-1-shaped. Quant brief ended with 10 numbered goals, 5 of them '(Merged into Goal N.)' tombstones, and 'Not doing: … in this first stage' still present.

Root cause #2 — append-only growth. Incremental final docs are 2.3-3x larger (quant spec 19.8k vs 6.0k words, 259 vs 103 reqs, 35 vs 12 decisions). Add-don't-rewrite + '(changed …)' markers + superseded decisions kept in full + per-stage Risks blocks accumulate; nothing consolidates.

Root cause #3 — cross-skill hand-off is incidental. All-at-once named null-hypothesis-testing in spec+architecture at the feature stage; incremental built its own protocol and cited the skill only at stage 2. No dev-team2 skill tells the agent to route a step to another installed skill.

Root cause #4 — no stop after architecture. 'Approved, go ahead' after an architecture approval led the agent to write docs/plan.md (both quant-incremental attempts) and, in the discarded attempt, to start coding on git branches. architecture-design says 'point the user to planning' but no planning skill exists.

Spec hygiene drifts under incremental: library names entered the spec (NumPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, Stable-Baselines3) via learning-oriented 'hand-built vs library' requirements; one turn drafted brief+spec together (turn 26, quant).

Non-discriminating assertions: Given/When/Then coverage, unique IDs, arch coverage = 0 uncovered, no lost IDs/decisions, approvals-only-after-user-approval passed in all 4 runs — the ID/traceability machinery works in both modes. The discriminating checks were brief goal count, vendor-free spec, gate discipline, null-hypothesis hand-off, final status.
Cost: incremental used 3.3x (RL) and 6.1x (quant) the agent time and 3.9x / 6.1x the cost (RL $7.98 vs $2.03; quant $18.07 vs $2.95).
